interpretation_policy.note: Source claims are historical evidence. Current injury, role, ownership and fantasy conclusions require fresh verification.
interpretation_policy.source_calibration: Direct injury/usage/depth-chart evidence is weighted above editorial conclusions such as must-draft, RB1 or projected goal-line dominance.

claims.source_claim: Jeanty left Sunday practice with an ankle sprain of unknown severity; the article lowers him in the rankings but keeps him immediately ahead of the also-injured Jeremiyah Love.

verification.summary: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Jeanty is on the mend without giving a return date. NFL reporting identifies the injury as an ankle sprain that is not expected to be long-term, while the return timeline remains unknown.

claims.interpretation: The injury itself is confirmed and materially relevant, but the available verification does not establish that Jeanty will miss the start of the regular season. Existing opponent-roster monitoring is sufficient.

claims.source_name_note: The current repository player record uses the display name Mike Washington; the source and Raiders reporting use Mike Washington Jr.
claims.source_claim: Because the article expects Jeanty to miss the start of the season, it upgrades Washington to a must-draft handcuff.

verification.summary: Official Raiders reporting confirms Washington received some of his first exclusive first-team reps while filling in for the injured Jeanty and impressed as a receiver. The premise that Jeanty will miss the start of the season is not currently established.

claims.interpretation: Washington has a real injury-opened opportunity signal, but it is contingent on Jeanty's availability and does not justify treating the lead role as earned. Because Washington is already league-owned, no free-agent watch target is created.

claims.source_claim: The article says Croskey-Merritt appears to be winning Washington's RB1 job, calls him the most explosive back on the team, and projects him for the majority of the goal-line work.

verification.summary: Washington's current official depth chart lists Croskey-Merritt first at running back ahead of Rachaad White. The Commanders held both Croskey-Merritt and White out of the Aug. 22 preseason game, and Croskey-Merritt was also held out of the Aug. 14 opener with numerous established starters. These facts support a high place in the hierarchy but do not independently prove that he will receive a majority of goal-line work.

claims.interpretation: The RB1/hierarchy portion is materially supported by current official team evidence; the goal-line-share assertion remains projection. Existing opponent-roster monitoring is sufficient and no manual watch target is needed.

durable_derivation_note: No new player-role-watch, Todo or qualitative baseline is required. All three players are league-owned and opponent rosters are already part of the intended Daily Monitoring population.
